newsitem.title: USA: Southwest Air's Q3, Q4 hurt by taxes, fuel costs.
newsitem.headline: Southwest Air's Q3, Q4 hurt by taxes, fuel costs.

text.p: Southwest Airlines Co's chairman and chief executive officer Herb Kelleher said on Wednesday that higher fuel costs, the reimposition of a 10 percent excise tax and a fuel tax were hurting efforts to keep costs down.

"Put all those things together and that produces a very heavy cost burden for the third quarter and I think probably the fourth quarter," Kelleher told Reuters in an interview. "Costs look heavy. They really do."
Kelleher said those additional costs were hitting the industry as a whole but stressed that Southwest's business remains strong.
"Load factors look good, bookings look good. That part of it looks strong," Kelleher said.
He did not give further details.
Kelleher estimated the total additional costs represented by the excise tax, the fuel tax and fuel costs rising about 20 cents a gallon amounted to about $128 million per quarter.
The 10 percent federal excise passenger tax was restored in late August and the federal transportation tax stands at 4.3 cents per gallon.
Kelleher said jet fuel costs have gone up by about 30 percent since the middle of June.
Southwest's costs per available seat mile rose to 7.49 cents in the first half of 1996, up 6.1 percent from 1995 levels, but the airline still posted its best-ever quarter in the second quarter.

Kelleher said Southwest was taking a close look at its operations in order to prevent costs from creeping higher. "It's a battle to keep it going and every once in a while you have to refocus on it a little more meticulously," he said.
Those efficiency efforts are focused on Southwest's reservatons system, purchasing agreements and maintenance operations.
"There is a cost war going on in the industry .... We have to stay fit, lean and mean," Kelleher said.
